newsitem.title: FRANCE: French car orders fell 10 pct in Dec - Peugeot.
newsitem.headline: French car orders fell 10 pct in Dec - Peugeot.

text.p: Orders for new cars fell 10 percent in France in December, matching November's drop after the expiry at the end of September of a state rebate scheme, Thierry Armangaud, sales director for Automobiles Peugeot, part of PSA Peugeot Citroen, told the newspaper La Tribune.
"We're paying now for the orders pulled forward by customers to before the end of September," Armangaud said.

He reiterated that the group expects a 10 percent drop in new car sales in 1997 to 1.93 million or 1.94 million units from 2.13 million in 1996. But he said 1997 would not show the ups and downs caused in 1996 by the rebate scheme's distortions.
"There's nothing that leads us to expect government assistance measures for the auto industry," he said.

The French carmakers' association CCFA on Thursday reported that 1996 sales rose 10.5 percent after a 1.8 percent gain in December. It estimated the rebate scheme accounted for 700,000 car sales in the year to October 1996 and for between 225,000 and 250,000 sales in the first nine months of calendar 1996.
